summary: Working in the geospatial space is tough: some days we're looking at the profile of the land, other days at the quality of the data, and other days yet the qualitative shape of spreading fire itself. Our app, Overheaters, unify these distinct workflows into one web app that allows professionals to take quick glances, leading to faster and more informed decisions specifically within Central Kalimantan, a region historically ravaged by forest fires. We harmonize the data by fitting a linear regression model onto historic MODIS data validated against modern day VIIRS observations that overlap with Aqua, creating an even scale across two centuries supported by previous work by Zheng et al,. 2026 and Li et al,. 2018. The app itself allows the user to draw a polygon over different layers, similar to a typical GIS app, and analyze spectral indices in a graph, with the unique option to place Savitzky-Golay smoothing in preparation for machine learning and data science applications. In all, we hope this web app offers a better, slightly-more-convinient-way, to help humans and nature live in harmony.
